summary: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are international master's programmes designed and delivered jointly by at least three higher education institutions from at least three countries, funded through Erasmus+ grants to those institutions. Students from anywhere in the world can apply if they hold a bachelor's degree (or are in their final year and will graduate before the programme starts). Applicants apply directly to the consortium running the programme they choose. Some programmes offer scholarships to the best-ranked students.
eligibility_notes:
You must hold a bachelor's degree (first degree) or be in your final year of bachelor's studies and graduate before the master's starts. A bachelor's-equivalent level of learning can also qualify if it is officially recognised under the national legislation and practice of the country that awards the degree. Students from all over the world are welcome.

Each programme sets its own entry requirements, subjects, teaching language and scholarship availability, shown on its own website. The scheme pages read state no age limit, no work-experience rule, no nationality limit for applying and no language test at scheme level.

For scholarships (Programme Guide): the scholarship is for full-time students; a student who already received an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship cannot receive another; and no more than 10% of the scholarships of a programme may go to candidates of the same nationality (this does not apply to top-up scholarships). Not every programme offers scholarships: some have no scholarships because their funding has ended or because they temporarily use the Erasmus Mundus name after funding.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work-experience requirement are stated on the scheme pages read.
funding_summary: Where a programme offers a scholarship, the Erasmus+ page says it covers participation costs and contributes to travel, visa costs and a living allowance. The Programme Guide sets the scholarship at a maximum of EUR 1,400 per month for the length of the programme (12, 18 or 24 months), to cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs, paid in full and only to full-time students. It can be reduced if prior learning is recognised, with a minimum of one academic year. Projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs to scholarship holders, and cannot charge application fees. Students without a scholarship are not covered by these rules and should check each programme's website for what they must pay.
programmes_note: Master's level only, 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits; 12, 18 or 24 months). The catalogue can be filtered by keyword, country, duration and credits, participating university, year of project selection (2018 to 2026) and field of study (for example Agro, AI, Food, Mech, Nucl, Space, Water, Art, Chemistry, Economic Sciences, Education, Environmental and Geosciences, History, Information Science and Engineering, Information Technology, Med, Law, Life Sciences, Literature, Mathematics, Physics, Political Science, Psychology, Social Sciences and Humanities). The catalogue read on 2026-11-13 listed 226 programmes over 12 pages of 20; the first 25 are included here.
institutions_note: Each Joint Master is run by a consortium of at least 3 institutions from at least 3 countries, with associated partners from academia and beyond. The consortium for each programme and its participating universities are shown on the programme's website, reached from the catalogue. Students must study in at least two countries during the programme (see the after-award steps).

summary.detail: Integrated international master's of 1 to 2 academic years (60, 90 or 120 ECTS), typically combining study periods, research, traineeship and thesis preparation and defence. Graduates receive either a joint degree (one certificate issued on behalf of at least two institutions) or multiple degrees (at least two certificates from two institutions in the consortium), as set out in the study agreement signed at the start. Teaching language is set by each programme.
summary.source_text: Jointly designed and delivered by a group of higher education institutions

benefits.limit_text: Participation costs covered by a scholarship, where the programme offers one
benefits.conditions: Programme Guide: projects cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs to scholarship holders. Not every programme offers scholarships; students without one should check the programme website.

benefits.limit_text: Scholarship of up to EUR 1,400 per month for the length of the programme (maximum is EUR 1,400 x number of months of the programme)
benefits.conditions: Paid in full only to full-time students and covers the whole programme; reduced if prior learning is recognised, with a minimum of one academic year. The amount is a combined contribution to travel, visa, installation and subsistence costs.

benefits.limit_text: Contribution to travel costs from the scholarship (no separate amount stated)
benefits.conditions: Included in the EUR 1,400 per month; no separate travel amount is stated.

benefits.limit_text: Contribution to visa costs and installation costs from the scholarship (no separate amount stated)
benefits.conditions: Included in the EUR 1,400 per month.

benefits.limit_text: Top-up scholarships for students from eligible third countries in regions 1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11
benefits.conditions: The Programme Guide mentions up to 18 NDICI-funded and up to 3 IPA III-funded scholarships; amounts of the top-ups are not stated on the page read.

benefits.limit_text: Special needs support for students with disabilities, from EUR 3,000 to EUR 60,000
benefits.conditions: Applicants request a maximum of two unit costs at the highest level (2 x EUR 60,000) at application stage.

benefits.limit_text: Not listed separately; subsistence and installation costs are part of the monthly scholarship
benefits.conditions: Students without a scholarship should check the programme website.

benefits.limit_text: Not mentioned on the scheme pages read

requirements.text: The scheme pages name no document list. Each master's website lists the documents, entry requirements and application steps with and without a scholarship, so check the programme before applying.

Proof that you hold a bachelor's degree (first degree) or an officially recognised equivalent, or that you are in your last year and will graduate before the master's starts. The accepted form of proof is set by each programme.

application_steps.title: Search the catalogue and pick a programme
application_steps.detail: Browse the Erasmus Mundus catalogue with its filters (field, country, duration, university, year of selection). Each entry links to the programme's official website, which gives course details, partner universities, entry requirements and application steps with and without a scholarship.

application_steps.title: Check entry rules and scholarship availability on the programme site
application_steps.detail: Entry requirements, subjects, teaching language and whether scholarships exist are set by each programme. Some programmes have no scholarships because their funding period has ended. The catalogue advises contacting the consortium directly with questions.

application_steps.title: Apply directly to the institution running the programme
application_steps.detail: There is no central application. Applications usually run between October and January for courses starting the following academic year. Selected programmes cannot charge application fees (Programme Guide).

application_steps.title: The consortium selects students
application_steps.detail: Selection is the sole responsibility of the consortium and must be organised transparently, impartially and equitably. Scholarships go to the best-ranked students worldwide, and no more than 10% of a programme's scholarships may go to the same nationality (except top-ups). The scheme pages do not describe criteria, interviews or dates; these are on each programme's site.

application_steps.title: Sign the Student Agreement at enrolment
application_steps.detail: Each student signs a Student Agreement with the consortium when enrolling; the template must be published on the programme website. It sets out whether you receive a joint degree or multiple degrees.

application_steps.title: Complete study periods in at least two countries
application_steps.detail: All enrolled students, with or without a scholarship, must complete at least two study periods in two countries, at least one in an EU Member State or associated third country, and both different from the country of residence at enrolment. Each period is at least one semester (30 ECTS, or 20 ECTS for 60-ECTS programmes). Virtual mobility cannot replace these periods.

fetch_problems: The catalogue pages were read as summaries; only pages 1 and 2 of the 12 listing pages were opened, so only 25 of 226 programmes are named. Programme websites were not opened.
The Programme Guide page does not state its edition year; its call ID (ERASMUS-EDU-2026-PEX-EMJM-MOB) suggests 2026.
notes: The catalogue read on 2026-11-13 listed 226 programmes (stored data said 218).

The EUR 1,400 per month figure is from the Programme Guide Erasmus Mundus action page; the Erasmus+ student pages give no amounts. Programmes may state their own figures; editors should check a programme site before quoting it as the amount a student gets.
